collection: TOEFL iBT 2026 original short conversation practice
note: Six original conversations with two questions each. Requires supervised live delivery; recorded audio remains outstanding. Keep scripts, answers and explanations out of learner view.
examinerInstructions: Two readers perform each conversation at a natural pace. Then present its two questions and four written choices per question. Award one classroom practice point for each correct answer. These points have no TOEFL scale conversion.

examinerScript.speaker: Student
examinerScript.line: I booked a camera for our field project, but the desk says it is still with another group. We leave tomorrow.

examinerScript.speaker: Assistant
examinerScript.line: Their return is due this afternoon. I can put your name first on the waiting list.

examinerScript.speaker: Student
examinerScript.line: I’m worried about leaving this until the last minute. Is there anything I can use if it doesn’t come back?

examinerScript.speaker: Assistant
examinerScript.line: There is a simpler model available now. It has fewer controls, but it will take the still photographs you described.

examinerScript.speaker: Student
examinerScript.line: That would cover our needs. Could you show me how to use it?

examinerScript.speaker: Assistant
examinerScript.line: Of course. We can sort out the loan form after the demonstration.

examinerScript.speaker: Nneka
examinerScript.line: We reserved Room Four for our practice debate, but I’ve just seen a notice saying it is a silent study room.

examinerScript.speaker: Jonah
examinerScript.line: Then our booking won’t help much. We need to speak at normal volume.

examinerScript.speaker: Nneka
examinerScript.line: The group room in the library is free later, though it only holds six people.

examinerScript.speaker: Jonah
examinerScript.line: There are five of us. Could we move the practice back an hour?

examinerScript.speaker: Nneka
examinerScript.line: I can, but I should check with everyone else before changing anything.

examinerScript.speaker: Jonah
examinerScript.line: Send the group a message. If they agree, I’ll reserve the library room.

examinerScript.speaker: Student
examinerScript.line: The campus bus hasn’t arrived, and I’m supposed to be at the museum for my placement this morning.

examinerScript.speaker: Friend
examinerScript.line: There’s road work near the south gate. The bus is using the east gate today.

examinerScript.speaker: Student
examinerScript.line: I didn’t see the notice. If I walk over there now, I might still be late.

examinerScript.speaker: Friend
examinerScript.line: Call your placement supervisor while you walk. At least they’ll know what has happened.

examinerScript.speaker: Student
examinerScript.line: Good point. I have the number in my confirmation email.

examinerScript.speaker: Friend
examinerScript.line: And check the transport page later. It says the change may continue tomorrow.

examinerScript.speaker: Amara
examinerScript.line: Our poster has all the results, but I can hardly read the labels from a few steps away.

examinerScript.speaker: David
examinerScript.line: I was trying to fit every measurement onto one page.

examinerScript.speaker: Amara
examinerScript.line: Do we need that much detail on the poster itself? We could put the full table in a handout.

examinerScript.speaker: David
examinerScript.line: That would leave room for larger charts. I’m reluctant to lose information, though.

examinerScript.speaker: Amara
examinerScript.line: We wouldn’t lose it. Visitors who want the details could take a handout, and everyone else could see the main pattern clearly.

examinerScript.speaker: David
examinerScript.line: All right. I’ll simplify the poster and keep the complete table in a separate sheet.

examinerScript.speaker: Student
examinerScript.line: I’ve signed up for the writing workshop, but it overlaps with the first half of my laboratory session.

examinerScript.speaker: Tutor
examinerScript.line: The workshop is repeated next week. Would that session fit?

examinerScript.speaker: Student
examinerScript.line: Yes, but the registration page says it is full.

examinerScript.speaker: Tutor
examinerScript.line: Ask the organiser whether there is a waiting list. People sometimes cancel.

examinerScript.speaker: Student
examinerScript.line: Would you advise skipping the first part of the laboratory session instead?

examinerScript.speaker: Tutor
examinerScript.line: No. That is when the safety briefing takes place. Try the waiting list first.

examinerScript.speaker: Researcher
examinerScript.line: The catalogue lists the town plan under its old name. I searched using the current name and found nothing.

examinerScript.speaker: Librarian
examinerScript.line: That happens with historical records. The catalogue keeps the name printed on the original document.

examinerScript.speaker: Researcher
examinerScript.line: So I shouldn’t assume that an empty search means we have no material?

examinerScript.speaker: Librarian
examinerScript.line: Exactly. Try earlier names and alternative spellings. I can show you the place-name index.

examinerScript.speaker: Researcher
examinerScript.line: That would help. I need maps from before the boundary change.

examinerScript.speaker: Librarian
examinerScript.line: The index notes those changes too. Let’s begin there before searching the map collection again.

questions.subject: Listening
questions.learningObjective: Interpret the purpose, details, intent or implied meaning of a short two-speaker conversation.
questions.prompt: Why does the student speak to the assistant?
options: To find an alternative camera for a trip.
To complain about the quality of some photographs.
To ask for extra time to return equipment.
To join another group’s field project.
questions.answer: To find an alternative camera for a trip.
questions.explanation: The booked camera is unavailable and the student needs equipment before departure.

questions.subject: Listening
questions.learningObjective: Interpret the purpose, details, intent or implied meaning of a short two-speaker conversation.
questions.prompt: What will the assistant most likely do next?
options: Call the group that has the booked camera.
Cancel the student’s field trip.
Demonstrate the simpler camera.
Process a repair request.
questions.explanation: The student asks for a demonstration, and the assistant agrees to give it before the paperwork.

questions.subject: Listening
questions.learningObjective: Interpret the purpose, details, intent or implied meaning of a short two-speaker conversation.
questions.prompt: What problem do Nneka and Jonah identify?
options: Their group is too large for the library room.
Their reserved room is unsuitable for discussion.
They have forgotten the date of the debate.
They cannot find their booking confirmation.
questions.answer: Their reserved room is unsuitable for discussion.
questions.explanation: A silent study room is unsuitable for a spoken debate.

questions.subject: Listening
questions.learningObjective: Interpret the purpose, details, intent or implied meaning of a short two-speaker conversation.
questions.prompt: What must happen before Jonah reserves the library room?
options: The debate topic must be approved.
Room Four must be repaired.
More students must join the group.
The other group members must agree to the later time.
questions.answer: The other group members must agree to the later time.
questions.explanation: Jonah offers to reserve the alternative only if the group agrees to the time change.

questions.subject: Listening
questions.learningObjective: Interpret the purpose, details, intent or implied meaning of a short two-speaker conversation.
questions.prompt: Why has the student missed the bus at the usual stop?
options: The museum has changed its opening hours.
The student has the wrong placement date.
Road work has changed the bus route.
The bus service has ended for the term.
questions.answer: Road work has changed the bus route.
questions.explanation: Road work has moved the bus route to the east gate.

questions.subject: Listening
questions.learningObjective: Interpret the purpose, details, intent or implied meaning of a short two-speaker conversation.
questions.prompt: What does the friend advise the student to do immediately?
options: Tell the placement supervisor about the delay.
Wait at the south gate for another bus.
Ask the museum to cancel the placement.
Walk the entire way to the museum.
questions.answer: Tell the placement supervisor about the delay.
questions.explanation: The friend recommends calling the supervisor while walking to the correct gate.

questions.subject: Listening
questions.learningObjective: Interpret the purpose, details, intent or implied meaning of a short two-speaker conversation.
questions.prompt: What change does Amara suggest for the poster?
options: Add more measurements to the main chart.
Print a smaller version of the same layout.
Remove the results from the presentation.
Move detailed data to a separate handout.
questions.answer: Move detailed data to a separate handout.
questions.explanation: Amara proposes a handout for the full table so the poster can be clearer.

questions.subject: Listening
questions.learningObjective: Interpret the purpose, details, intent or implied meaning of a short two-speaker conversation.
questions.prompt: Why is David initially reluctant to change the poster?
options: He thinks handouts are forbidden.
He does not want to omit information.
He has not finished collecting the data.
He prefers speaking without visual aids.
questions.answer: He does not want to omit information.
questions.explanation: David explicitly says he is reluctant to lose information.

questions.subject: Listening
questions.learningObjective: Interpret the purpose, details, intent or implied meaning of a short two-speaker conversation.
questions.prompt: Which solution does the tutor recommend?
options: Miss the laboratory safety briefing.
Attend the workshop without registering.
Ask about a waiting list for the later workshop.
Drop the laboratory course entirely.
questions.answer: Ask about a waiting list for the later workshop.
questions.explanation: The tutor recommends seeking a place in the repeated workshop.

questions.subject: Listening
questions.learningObjective: Interpret the purpose, details, intent or implied meaning of a short two-speaker conversation.
questions.prompt: Why does the tutor reject arriving late to the laboratory session?
options: The opening includes essential safety information.
The writing workshop finishes too early.
The laboratory closes before the workshop begins.
The student has already attended the workshop.
questions.answer: The opening includes essential safety information.
questions.explanation: The tutor identifies the safety briefing as the reason not to miss the beginning.

questions.subject: Listening
questions.learningObjective: Interpret the purpose, details, intent or implied meaning of a short two-speaker conversation.
questions.prompt: Why did the researcher’s initial catalogue search fail?
options: The maps had all been borrowed.
The catalogue used a historical place name.
The archive contained only photographs.
The researcher searched the wrong century.
questions.answer: The catalogue used a historical place name.
questions.explanation: The catalogue retains the name on the original plan.

questions.subject: Listening
questions.learningObjective: Interpret the purpose, details, intent or implied meaning of a short two-speaker conversation.
questions.prompt: What does the librarian imply about a search with no results?
options: The archive should discard older catalogues.
The requested material is definitely missing.
Only staff may search the map collection.
A different search term may reveal relevant material.
questions.answer: A different search term may reveal relevant material.
questions.explanation: The librarian suggests earlier names and alternative spellings rather than treating an empty search as proof of absence.
